raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
### Motivation

Native CPU offloading computes CPU cache capacity from each worker's KV cache tensors. Under pipeline parallelism, workers may own different numbers or types of layers, so different PP ranks can derive different CPU offload chunk counts.

The scheduler uses the first worker's KV cache config, while workers build offloading specs from their local configs. If the scheduler-side chunk count is larger than a worker's local CPU buffer capacity, offloaded chunk ids can exceed that worker's allocated CPU cache range.

This is a stability fix, not just a consistency one: when an out-of-range id is actually used, the failure is not an assertion — it is a SIGSEGV inside the CUDA driver, 10–24 minutes into a run, with no traceback and nothing in the kernel log (second reproduction in #50821).

The divergence is not specific to uneven layer counts: it also occurs with a balanced pipeline when speculative decoding places the draft (MTP) layers on the last stage — both stages can own the same number of groups and the same
num_blocks and still compute different chunk counts.

### Runtime Validation

  I reproduced the issue with vLLM v0.26.0 using:

  - Model: `GLM-5.2-NVFP4`
  - `pipeline_parallel_size=4`
  - `tensor_parallel_size=1`
  - Native CPU offloading via `OffloadingConnector`
  - Prefix caching enabled
  - No SSD offloading

  Before the fix, different PP ranks computed different CPU offload block counts from their local KV cache tensors:

  ```text
  scheduler/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 35341
  worker/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 35341
  worker/rank1 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank2 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank3 CPU num_blocks: 36561
  ```
  This confirms the mismatch. Since the scheduler allocates CPU block IDs based on its own CPU block count, rank1/rank2 only had capacity for 34435 blocks while the scheduler could allocate IDs up to 35340. Those IDs would be outside rank1/rank2's CPU buffer range.

  After applying the fix, all PP ranks used the same unified minimum CPU block count:
  ```text
  scheduler CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank0 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank1 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank2 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  worker/rank3 CPU num_blocks: 34435
  ```
  The fixed server also started successfully and returned successful responses:

  GET /health -> 200
  POST /v1/completions -> 200

### Proposed Changes

- Compute the CPU offload chunk capacity for every worker KV cache config and take the minimum across workers, so the scheduler can never allocate an id beyond any worker's capacity. The unification lives in the offloading subsystem (`unify_cpu_offload_num_chunks` in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/config.py`) and reuses the CPU backend's own `cpu_offload_layout` sizing, so a worker's view and the scheduler's unified count cannot be derived differently. This also resolves the connector's own config when it is nested inside a MultiConnector, so the unification applies there too.
- Carry the unified count on the pre-existing `CacheConfig.num_cpu_blocks`  (no new field on `KVCacheConfig`): the engine core computes it where all worker configs are visible, and each worker recomputes the same value from the full `kv_cache_configs` list in `initialize_from_config`.
- Propagate it through `OffloadingConfig.num_cpu_blocks` into `CPUOffloadingSpec`.
- Reject out-of-range block ids in `compute_sub_block_ptrs` instead of computing a wild pointer (from @yqszxx, also open as #60061), turning a delayed SIGSEGV into an immediate ValueError.
- Thanks to @yqszxx, who rebased the original fix onto current main and contributed the CPU-tier geometry dedup and the bounds guard.

### Test Plan


```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector/test_config.py -q
# 76 passed
```

- `test_unify_cpu_offload_num_chunks_across_pp_stages` covers both PP stage orderings (including the one where the scheduler's source stage has more capacity) and asserts the scheduler config and every worker config resolve to the unified count.
- `test_unify_cpu_offload_num_chunks_balanced_pp_spec_decode` covers the balanced-PP + MTP case, where both stages own the same number of groups and the same num_blocks but different page sizes.

  Manual serving validation was also performed on vLLM v0.26.0 with GLM-5.2-NVFP4, pipeline_parallel_size=4, tensor_parallel_size=1, native CPU offloading, and prefix caching. Before the fix, worker CPU block counts differed across PP ranks. After the fix, all ranks used the unified CPU block count and the server returned successful /health and /v1/completions responses.

### Duplicate Work Check

I searched open vLLM PRs/issues for CPU offload combined with pipeline parallelism (keywords: `OffloadingConnector`, `num_cpu_blocks`, `worker_kv_bytes_per_block`, `row_stride`, `cpu_page_size`). Within that search, I could not find an existing PR that fixes the PP chunk-count consistency issue itself. The closest neighbors, which this PR does not
duplicate:

- #60061 carries the same `compute_sub_block_ptrs` bounds guard as a standalone PR (the guard commit here is from the same author, @yqszxx).
- #53271 adds a complementary pointer-level check in the same function, for a different root cause (padded MLA pages make the sub-block offsets drift even with in-range ids).

3. Test coverage: the PP test is parametrized over both stage orderings (including the one where the scheduler's source stage has more capacity than a later stage) and asserts the scheduler config and every worker config resolve to the unified count, both at the OffloadingConfig level and through CPUOffloadingSpec.num_chunks. 8ac5065ad7 adds a second test for the balanced-PP + spec-decode (MTP draft on the last stage) case from #50821, where both stages own the same number of groups and the same num_blocks but still diverge.

On CPU memory / throughput / latency: the tier stays capped by `cpu_bytes_to_use` (num_chunks is the min over workers, so the region is never larger than before), sizing happens once at init, and no hot path changes.
Under TP-only (PP=1) all workers compute identical values, so behavior is unchanged there.

@StellaH-ter This fixes a case we hit independently. Since the PR has been idle since the conflicts mergify flagged on 2026-08-04, I rebased it onto current main: `yqszxx/vllm:fix-kv-offload-pp-num-chunks` (`ddba7c8024`, on upstream `bf01fc4a31`). Your commit is the first of three with authorship intact; the other two collapse the duplicated capacity arithmetic in `get_cpu_offload_num_blocks`, which had drifted from the real computation, and add the bounds check below. Pulling that branch or retargeting this PR's head to it may be quicker.

Details and a second reproduction are in #50821; two points that may be useful for the description:

- The divergence also occurs with a **balanced** pipeline, when speculative decoding puts the draft (MTP) layers on the last stage. Both stages can own the same number of groups and the same `num_blocks` and still compute different chunk counts.
- When an out-of-range id is actually used, it is not an assertion — it is a `SIGSEGV` inside the CUDA driver, 10–24 minutes into a run, with no traceback and nothing in the kernel log. So this is a stability fix, not just a consistency one.

One scope suggestion: unifying the count fixes this instance, but `compute_sub_block_ptrs` in `vllm/v1/kv_offload/cpu/gpu_worker.py` still computes `base_ptr + id * row_stride` with no check against `tensor.shape[0]`, so an id that is out of range for any other reason remains a silent out-of-bounds host write that surfaces much later as an unexplained worker death. A cheap assert there would have turned a ~15-minute mystery segfault into an immediate traceback. It is the third commit on that branch, separable if you would rather keep this PR to the capacity fix.

Hi @yqszxx — thanks for the second reproduction and the rebase, and sorry for the delay. I've adopted your branch onto current main with your authorship intact (the geometry dedup + the compute_sub_block_ptrs guard).

Agreed the divergence isn't specific to uneven layer counts: the unification takes the min over all worker configs, so the balanced-PP + MTP case is covered too. I added a regression test for it (8ac5065ad7), next to the uneven-layer
one. The min is the actual fix — it keeps the scheduler from handing out ids beyond any worker's capacity — and the guard is defense-in-depth on top.

I also addressed the maintainer review: the unification now lives in the offloading subsystem (reusing cpu_offload_layout), and num_cpu_blocks was dropped from KVCacheConfig.

Two related-work notes for the maintainers:

- row_stride / cpu_page_size still differ across PP stages. I don't think it should block this PR; I'll file it as a separate issue (same
  geometry-assumption family as #53607 / #56871 / #53042) and follow up with a PR once the layout semantics are agreed — it will need to coordinate with #59546, which restructures SharedOffloadRegion.
- #53271 adds a complementary pointer-level bounds check in the same function, for a different root cause (padded MLA pages drift even with in-range ids, which the id-level guard here cannot catch). The two overlap textually, so maintainers can decide how to land them; if the guard should live in #60061 instead of this PR, I can drop the commit on the next rebase.
